editorial:
Unpopular best friends PJ and Josie are tired of being ignored, so they invent a self-defense club just to get close to girls. What starts as a silly lie turns into a wild high school comedy where everyone starts fighting for real. The movie is loud, rude, and packed with jokes that land fast. You feel the awkward energy of two teens who want attention but have no plan.

The cast sells every ridiculous moment, especially the leads, who make you root for them even when they are being terrible. The pacing rarely slows down, so you are always moving from one funny mess to the next. Some jokes are crude and the story gets messy near the end, but the heart keeps it fun. If you like teen comedies with chaos and sharp timing, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, PJ and Josie admit their club started as a lie to get close to girls. The truth causes a huge fight at the football game, but the club members rally and beat the football players. PJ and Josie finally get honest with each other and the girls they like, ending with them together and the club still standing.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves bold teen comedies with sharp jokes and messy friendships.
